{"lessons": ["

How are you?

English has one \"you\". Italian has a friendly one and a polite one, so the question comes in three versions.

— Come stai? — Bene, grazie. E tu?— How are you? — Fine, thanks. And you?

Come stai? is for a friend, a relative or someone your own age. Come va? works with anyone, like \"how's it going?\". To a stranger or an older person, say Come sta?

To answer: bene (fine, well), molto bene (very well), così così (so-so). Then you return the question: E tu?

", "

Saying your name

— Come ti chiami? — Mi chiamo Léa.— What's your name? — My name is Léa.

You can also simply say Sono Léa, \"I'm Léa\". When you meet someone, add Piacere! Like \"nice to meet you\", it's the same for everyone: this word never changes.

By ear, two traps: chi sounds like \"kee\" (mi chiamo, \"mee KYAH-mo\") and ce sounds like \"cheh\" (piacere, \"pya-CHEH-reh\").
